# Automation with a clear human decision point

Reliable systems define what software may prepare, what evidence a person sees, and which actions
cannot happen without approval.
:::

{{< include _subnav.html >}}

::: {.ai-section}
## The approval policy

::: {.ai-grid}
::: {.ai-card}
### May be automatic

- Calculations and comparisons
- Research across approved records
- Suggested classifications
- Summaries and complete drafts
- Detection of missing or conflicting information
:::
::: {.ai-card}
### Requires a responsible person's approval

- Sending a message
- Submitting a form
- Scheduling or changing an event
- Creating, changing, or deleting a record
- Initiating a bank or card payment
:::
:::

## Controls built for the real workflow

Approval is only useful when the reviewer can see the proposed action, its destination, the source
information, and any uncertainty. A system should preserve an audit trail, stop when required
information is missing, and make exceptions more visible instead of hiding them.
